text: "I thought we got outskated. I thought we got outworked."  More on the #Buffalo #Sabres' late implosion in their loss to the Ottawa Senators and the strong effort from goalie Colten Ellis they wasted:  www.buffalohockeybeat.com/sabres-implo...
Sabres lose 2-1.
Michael Amadio scores at 16:51 on a play similar to the one Colten Ellis stymied earlier in the game. Senators up 2-1.
Getting "The A-Team" theme on the organ again!
Final: Sabres fall 2-1
2-1 Senators  Michael Amadio from the left circle with 3:09 left in the period.

I came away more impressed with how the Senators pressured all over the ice and gave Buffalo's defensemen little time and limited outlets to get their way up the ice. Obviously very frustrating for Buffalo and it wore them down, but if Ottawa plays more like that regularly they'll be a huge pain
If you noticed Ryan McLeod look bad on Ottawa's tying goal, he had just one more shift after that in the final 8 1/2 minutes for 13 seconds according to the game sheets

Sabres seemed slow and most of that is because they spent much of the game pursuing the Senators in their own zone as they worked the puck around and generated shot attempts. Icing that lead to the tying goal came after that group was out for over a minute. Tough sledding.

Pretty simple sum-up from Lindy Ruff: They just weren't good enough tonight.   "I thought we got outskated, I thought we got outworked. We gave up six or seven odd-numbered rushes and the game-winning goal and an odd-numbered rush late... We had zero odd-numbered rushes."
Sabres threaten with Ellis pulled for the extra skater but are unable to get another past Ersson. Sens win it 2-1 in a gritty game
Michael Amadio got robbed early in the game and then he gives Ottawa a 2-1 lead with 3:09 to go in the third on a 3-on-2 after a feed by Stützle.

Bedard: "Blash is great. We love Blash, we love how he approaches us, how he coaches our team. I know on a personal note how much better of a hockey player he's made me. … He's given us the right message, the right formula, and we've got to go execute better for 60 minutes."
Jeff Blashill on Connor Bedard: "I thought he competed like crazy. For not every guy to follow that suit is not acceptable. I thought a lot of guys did, but you’ve got to have 20 going."
Blashill: "There was a lot of guys that competed their asses off, and I think there were a few guys that played at the end of their stick, and we can’t have that."
